_comment: gdbtools machine profile: what the target cannot report about itself. Needed where there is no QEMU monitor to ask and no device tree to read -- a real board behind a JTAG probe or an external gdbstub. Every field is OPTIONAL, but a field left out is simply not known: nothing substitutes a default for it, and whatever needed it either skips that step or refuses. Apply with $GDBTOOLS_PROFILE=FILE before gdb starts, or mid-session: kearly profile FILE. Individual $GDBTOOLS_* variables override matching fields. Numbers accept hex strings or ints.

_help.arch: x86_64 | arm64 | riscv64 -- informational; the real arch is auto-detected from the target
_help.ram_base / ram_size: physical RAM window; drives the Image-magic scan and the calibration sanity check
_help.entry_pa: pin the kernel image-base physical address. Required whenever the target cannot report it -- always on x86_64, whose decompressor relocates the image so there is no magic in memory to find it by
_help.scan: explicit physical scan ranges 'lo:hi' for the Image magic (overrides the ram-derived ranges)
_help.phys_window: [lo, hi] plausible image phys range, used only to sanity-check the computed offset. Left out, the check is skipped rather than run against some other board's range
_help.anchor: symbol where firmware enters the kernel (UEFI -> primary_entry / _start_kernel; default = image base)
_help.break_kind: sw | hw breakpoint at the entry (sw if the entry runs in place, hw if it gets overwritten)
_help.mmu: optional {reg, bit} to read the MMU-enable bit when the arch default register name does not apply
